question: Should exec denylist policy remain unioned across both `openclaw.json` and `exec-approvals.json`, or should one persisted surface be the canonical owner?
rationale: Both surfaces independently tighten privileged command authorization and introduce compatibility, upgrade, conflict, and operator-control semantics that code review cannot choose without product and security ownership intent.

options.title: Use One Canonical Surface
options.body: Keep denylist policy in one persisted owner and remove the parallel source to reduce drift and ambiguous operator control.

options.title: Keep Both Unioned Surfaces
options.body: Explicitly accept stricter-wins union semantics and require documented upgrade, conflict, hot-reload, and UI behavior.

recommendation.title: Use One Canonical Surface
recommendation.body: Keep denylist policy in one persisted owner and remove the parallel source to reduce drift and ambiguous operator control.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history shows direct ownership of the affected exec authorization paths, and the PR discussion already routes this contract decision there.
